newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Baltic Shipping to sell more assets to pay debts.
newsitem.headline: Baltic Shipping to sell more assets to pay debts.

text.p: Russia's financially-troubled Baltic Shipping Company plans to sell more assets to raise cash, a regional government official advising the firm said on Wednesday.

Dmitry Sergeyev, head of a government commission in charge of overseeing the ailing shipper, told a news conference that OAO Baltiiskoye Morskoye Parokhodstovo, or BMP, would seek to pay off domestic and foreign debts and stave off bankruptcy.
"Based on the information we have received, we think about 60 ships will stay in BMP ownership and under trust and we shall be able to preserve the company in this state," he said.
He said the St Petersburg administration was preparing to sell 280 billion roubles' worth of the company's land-based assets, including a hotel, printing house, meat-processing factory and offices.

The shipper, 29.7 percent state-owned and one of Russia's most prominent, has debts to foreign creditors of over $300 million and 23 of its ships docked in foreign ports have been seized by foreign creditors.
The company, which had 176 vessels at the start of this decade, is down to 66 ships, including the seized vessels.
It has been selling some ships to raise cash.
Sergeyev said eight billion roubles raised through the sales had gone to pay off wage arrears.
BMP's 1995 losses, stated according to Russian accounting standards, were nearly 216 billion roubles. It owes Russian creditors, including the state, 340 billion roubles.
